name: Ingersoll Rand Inc.

profile.description: Ingersoll Rand Inc. is a diversified industrial company providing mission-critical flow creation and life science and industrial solutions worldwide. It operates through two segments: Industrial Technologies & Services (compressors, blowers, vacuum systems, air treatment and power tools) and Precision & Science Technologies (pumps, fluid management, dosing and life sciences equipment). Formed from the 2020 combination of Gardner Denver and Ingersoll-Rand's Industrial segment, the company grows through its IRX execution system and a steady cadence of bolt-on acquisitions.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Innovation Track Record (2/3): The 2020 Gardner Denver / IR Industrial combination redefined the company, and FY2025 revenue of $7.65B is nearly double the $3.97B reported in FY2020 on the back of dozens of bolt-ons, with Lone Star Blower closed in Q3 2026 and a US pump maker closing October 30, 2026 [1][2]. AI Deployment (0/2): The Q3 2026 release and annual report contain no quantified AI product revenue or AI-driven cost savings [1][4]. Market Share Leadership (1/2): Meaningful positions in compressors, blowers and precision pumps, but it competes with category leader Atlas Copco rather than leading outright. Product Pipeline (1/2): Q3 orders jumped 21% (18% organic) to $2.35B, including a ~$195M engineered-to-order award, giving visibility but without named next-gen product launches [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): IR does not break out R&D as a line item and its growth model is acquisition-led rather than R&D-led [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): The stated purpose, 'Lean on us to help you make life better,' connects industrial equipment to efficiency and sustainability but is generic enough to fit most industrial peers [4]. Community Impact (1/2): The company reports multi-year sustainability milestones, a 2025 S&P Global CSA score of 82 and an MSCI AA rating held since 2022, which reflect general corporate programs rather than distinctive, dollar-quantified community investment [5][6]. Employee Retention (0/2): Management describes an ownership culture where 'every employee thinks and acts like an owner,' but no audited voluntary turnover or tenure data was found [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful open-market insider purchases were found; the board instead extended CEO Reynal's employment agreement on October 30, 2026 [3].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated on the Growth-sleeve formula (10 weight units). D/E of 46.4% beats the 70% target (1.00) and ROE of 13.4% is just under the 15% target (0.89, 2x weight) [7]. Revenue growth of 5.6% YoY scores 0.85, while the FY2020-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 14.0% (derived from $3.97B to $7.65B reported revenue) scores 1.00 at 2x weight [2]. Forward P/E of 20.4 scores 0.99 and the TTM profit margin of 17.2% scores 0.86, though TTM earnings are flattered by ILC Dover recoveries and IEEPA tariff refunds [1][7]. FMP's forward PEG of 2.55 scores only 0.23 at 2x weight, giving 7.94/10, rounded to 8 [8]. Liquidity is ample: 4.39M shares x $80.05 = ~$351M of daily traded value.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Ingersoll Rand builds physical compressors, blowers, vacuum pumps and fluid-handling equipment that must be engineered, manufactured and serviced on site, so there is no plausible AI substitution path for its core revenue [2]. AI data center construction is a demand tailwind for compressed air, vacuum and thermal management equipment, and Q3 2026 IT&S orders rose 25% with a 1.17x segment book-to-bill [1]. The modest risk is that AI-enabled predictive maintenance by third parties could pressure aftermarket economics over time. AI Opportunity (0/1): The company does not disclose any quantified revenue from AI-specific products or services [1].

infinite_game.summary: Ingersoll Rand plays a disciplined, owner-minded game, but its purpose is generic and its growth engine is M&A, which Sinek would see as more finite than cause-driven. The broad employee-ownership culture and CEO continuity are genuine strengths. The company is only six years old in its current form and has yet to show a cause-driven reinvention.

just_cause.analysis: 'Make life better' describes good intentions but not a distinctive future state people would sacrifice for, and it does not visibly steer strategy beyond portfolio selection [4]. The current company was created in 2020, so the cause has not been tested across leadership transitions or decades [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: IR's defining cultural practice is broad-based ownership; the lead independent director credits Reynal with building 'a culture where every employee thinks and acts like an owner' and a deep bench of leaders [3]. Ownership mindset is codified alongside the IRX business system in the annual report's guiding principles, and leadership has been stable for nearly a decade [4].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Management's public framing centers on its own execution system and share gains rather than learning from rivals such as Atlas Copco [1][4]. No commentary was found that frames competitors as worthy rivals that improve IR.

existential_flexibility.analysis: The 2020 merger and the push into life sciences through P&ST, where orders and revenue grew low double digits in Q3 2026, show real portfolio evolution [1]. These moves extend adjacent flow-control markets rather than abandoning a core business, so they count as incremental flexibility.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Leadership kept funding acquisitions and organic growth investment through 2023-2026 while deleveraging to 1.6x net debt/EBITDA, and pursued roughly $425M of ILC Dover recoveries rather than absorbing the loss [1]. It also leans heavily on buybacks ($350M in Q3 plus a new $2B authorization), which Sinek would view as a more finite use of capital [1].

investment_thesis: Ingersoll Rand is a high-quality industrial compounder with a clean balance sheet (46% D/E, 1.6x net leverage) and 28% adjusted EBITDA margins [1][7]. Q3 2026 orders surged 21% (18% organic), and management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 5.5%-7.0% with adjusted EPS of $3.58-$3.70 excluding tariff refunds [1].
thesis_continued: The score is capped by an acquisition-led model with little measurable AI or R&D differentiation, a generic purpose, and a forward PEG of 2.55 that leaves limited valuation upside [8]. The order acceleration needs to convert into organic revenue growth above the 2%-3.5% guided range before the shares look compelling on this framework.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 orders up 21% (18% organic) with a 1.17x IT&S book-to-bill point to accelerating organic revenue in 2027 [1]
$2B added to the buyback authorization plus $3.9B of liquidity to fund continued bolt-on M&A such as Lone Star Blower and the pending US pump maker [1]
Life Sciences orders and revenue growing low double digits, shifting mix toward higher-margin P&ST businesses [1]
key_risks: TTM earnings are flattered by one-time ILC Dover recoveries and IEEPA tariff refunds; underlying adjusted EBITDA excluding refunds grew only 1% in Q3 [1]
Organic revenue growth guided at just 2%-3.5% for 2026, leaving growth dependent on acquisitions and integration execution [1]
Forward PEG of 2.55 and a 20x forward P/E leave little margin for an industrial slowdown [7][8]

backlog.note: Backlog not disclosed. Book-to-bill shown is the 9-month 2026 figure ($6,366M orders / $5,961M revenue), used as a TTM proxy. Q3 alone was ~1.14x, led by IT&S at 1.17x and a ~$195M engineered-to-order award.
